channel.title: News Today — Smart AI News Portal
channel.description: বাংলাদেশ, ভারত ও বিশ্বের সর্বশেষ খবর — স্বয়ংক্রিয়ভাবে আপডেটেড

item.title: ভারতীয় মন্ত্রীর এপস্টিনের সঙ্গে সাক্ষাতের ছবি ঘিরে রাজনৈতিক বিতর্ক
item.description: বিরোধী দলগুলো হরদীপ সিং পুরির সঙ্গে জেফরি এপস্টিনের একটি বৈঠকের ছবি প্রকাশ্যে আসার পর তীব্র প্রতিক্রিয়া জানিয়েছে। ছবিগুলোতে দুজনকে একটি টেবিলে পাশাপাশি বসে আলোচনা করতে দেখা গেছে।

item.title: Mexican ex-prosecutor faces treason charges over US drug raid
item.description: César Jáuregui Moreno is facing treason accusations for allegedly permitting American personnel to participate in an April drug lab operation.

item.title: Tesla begins Optimus robot manufacturing amid declining profits
item.description: Tesla has initiated production of its Optimus humanoid robot in California while reporting a 43 percent drop in profit. The company faced surging expenses and flat revenue due to investments in AI and autonomous driving.

item.title: Startup Recursive introduces Flint, an AI-built coding model
item.description: Recursive has unveiled Flint, a compact coding model designed primarily by its own artificial intelligence system. The free software serves as a trial for self-improving AI technology.

item.title: Pope requires no additional medical care following lung surgery
item.description: Medical tests verified that the Pope's condition involved localized lung adenocarcinoma. He does not need any further treatments after undergoing the procedure.

item.title: Tesla reports flat third-quarter revenue despite Roadster reveal
item.description: Tesla announced its Q3 financial results on Wednesday, showing static revenue of $28.0 billion and a net income of $1.7 billion. The earnings report followed a demonstration of the company's Roadster vehicle.

item.title: Automattic implements staff layoffs amid leadership changes
item.description: Automattic has started staff reductions across divisions like WordPress.com and enterprise operations following recent executive exits and board reorganization. Additional reductions may occur as the firm works to strengthen its finances.

item.title: US diplomatic efforts unlikely to bring immediate peace to Ukraine
item.description: Current American diplomatic initiatives provide minimal expectation for a near-term resolution to the conflict. Russian leader Vladimir Putin currently experiences no urgency to halt the fighting.

item.title: Transfer Rumors: Chelsea Targets Ayari and Arsenal Weighs Gyokeres Move
item.description: Chelsea has set its sights on Brighton midfielder Yasin Ayari. Meanwhile, Real Madrid and Barcelona monitor Aston Villa's Johan Manzambi, and Arsenal considers parting ways with forward Viktor Gyokeres.

item.title: Meta Receives Record $25 Billion Penalty Over Data Privacy Misstatements
item.description: The parent company of Facebook faces a record $25 billion financial penalty regarding user data privacy. This punishment surpasses a previous $18 billion legal settlement reached with California regulators.

item.title: Audio Maker Bose Purchases Competitor Skullcandy to Expand Market Reach
item.description: Bose has officially completed the purchase of rival audio brand Skullcandy to broaden its customer base. The acquisition follows a recent collaboration where Skullcandy integrated Bose spatial audio features into its products.

item.title: Southwest Airlines Lowers 2026 Profit Projections Amid Rising Fuel Costs
item.description: Southwest Airlines reduced its financial outlook for 2026 because of climbing fuel expenses. This adjustment makes it the third major US airline to lower its profit guidance this month.

item.title: Drone Strike Debris at Saudi Oil Facility Leaves Two Workers Dead
item.description: Falling debris from a drone strike at a Saudi oil installation resulted in two fatalities involving citizens from Nepal and the Philippines. The Saudi Ministry reported that additional workers from Pakistan and India sustained injuries.

item.title: Cuba Claims US Pressures Nations Prior to UN Trade Embargo Vote
item.description: The Cuban government alleges that Washington is intimidating international governments with punitive measures. These threats reportedly aim to prevent nations from voting against the US trade embargo at the United Nations.

item.title: Former England Player Bertrand Leads Group in £87M AFC Wimbledon Bid
item.description: Ex-England international Ryan Bertrand is heading a group of investors offering an £87 million minority stake in League One club AFC Wimbledon.

item.title: General Motors Relies on AI and New Computing for Upcoming EV Platform
item.description: GM is introducing an advanced central computer and electrical system to rival Chinese EV makers and competitors like Tesla. This fourth-generation platform will launch in 2028 with the Cadillac Escalade IQ.

item.title: Fernandes Criticizes Carrick After Manchester United Defeat
item.description: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes pointed to manager Michael Carrick's tactical approach following a 4-1 Champions League loss against Como.

item.title: South Delhi Traffic Jams Caused by RTR Flyover Ramp Closure
item.description: Traffic backed up for a kilometre in South Delhi after the Vasant Vihar descending ramp of the RTR flyover closed for repairs, forcing vehicles onto service roads and affecting a major route to the airport and Gurugram.

item.title: হ্যারি রাজপরিবারের সঙ্গে সম্পর্ক স্বাভাবিক করতে চান
item.description: প্রিন্সেস ডায়ানার মৃত্যুর প্রভাব নিজের জীবনে কেমন পড়েছে, সে বিষয়ে একটি সাক্ষাৎকারে কথা বলেছেন হ্যারি। মাত্র ১২ বছর বয়সে সড়ক দুর্ঘটনায় তাঁর মা মারা যান।

item.title: Sydney Metro Line Southwest Extension Opens Next Week
item.description: The long-awaited southwest extension of Sydney's metro line is scheduled to open on Friday, October 30. This follows the closure of the former T3 heavy rail line more than two years ago.

item.title: Airbnb Bans Hosts From Requiring Chores Like Dishes and Trash
item.description: Airbnb has updated its house rules to prohibit hosts from demanding that guests complete tedious departure chores, such as washing dishes or taking out the garbage, for bookings made from November 20 onward.

item.title: Anthropic Launches Claude Duet AI Agent for Professionals
item.description: Anthropic has introduced Claude Duet, a new artificial intelligence agent aimed at small business owners and professionals. Released as a research preview, it serves as a standalone competitor to similar tools from OpenAI and Meta.

item.title: Nigerian Ebola Patient Visited Uganda Before Diagnosis
item.description: Authorities report that Nigeria's initial Ebola case, an Abuja-based diplomat's wife, previously took a holiday in Kampala.

item.title: General Motors Targets Two-Year Vehicle Production Cycle Using AI
item.description: General Motors plans to shorten its vehicle development timeline to roughly two years by increasing its reliance on artificial intelligence, software, and simulation technologies.

item.title: Meta Faces $25B Fine Following Cambridge Analytica Lawsuit
item.description: Following a court case examining its privacy policies, the social media corporation was directed to issue a $25 billion financial penalty.

item.title: Australian Politician Helen Haines Loses Both Legs in Crash
item.description: Lawmaker Helen Haines sustained severe injuries, resulting in the amputation of both legs after a vehicle struck her.

item.title: Former Candidate Ousted by Conservatives After Al Jazeera Exposé
item.description: The Conservative Party took action against a former election candidate who appeared in a 2021 undercover media probe into Turning Point UK.

item.title: Australia Faces Severe Defeat and Scrutiny in South Africa Test
item.description: Following a disastrous fourth-day display in the second Test against South Africa, Australia is staring at a potential loss. Several players now face intense pressure regarding their professional futures.

item.title: Zelensky Anticipates Discussions Involving Russia and US by November
item.description: The Ukrainian leader told reporters he engaged with US representatives following envoy Steve Witkoff's meeting with Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg.

item.title: Walmart Embraces AI Shoppers While Amazon Restricts Them
item.description: Unlike Amazon, which restricts automated systems, Walmart now allows AI agents to buy items for users with built-in financial limits and approvals.

item.title: Macron Condemns Foreign Officials Over Remarks on French Riots
item.description: The French president criticized Donald Trump and other international figures for political remarks regarding ongoing domestic demonstrations.

item.title: BJD Criticizes BJP for Targeting Naveen Over CJP Release Demand
item.description: The BJD condemned the BJP for personal attacks against Naveen following his call to release CJP figures, while the BJP accused him of inciting unrest.

item.title: Xbox Tests Cloud Gaming Options for Non-Subscribers
item.description: Microsoft's gaming division is trialing paid cloud streaming access for users who do not hold a standard Game Pass subscription.

item.title: Walmart to Introduce AI Shopping Assistants for Customers
item.description: Beginning next month, Walmart will permit users to integrate automated AI assistants into its online store. The platform will include controls enabling shoppers to establish financial boundaries and authorize transactions.

item.title: Apple Music Emphasizes Human Curation Amid AI Growth
item.description: Apple Music is highlighting human-made curation as a strategy to stand out in an industry increasingly dominated by artificial intelligence content.

item.title: New South Wales Legalizes Human Composting for Deceased
item.description: Legislators in New South Wales have approved Australia's first human composting regulations, offering a new alternative to traditional burial and cremation. Multiple members of parliament stated an intention to choose this method after death.

item.title: Indian Political Figures Released After Week in Custody
item.description: Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, two prominent figures from India's Cockroach Party, have regained their freedom following a week behind bars.

item.title: Kochi Pharmaceutical Company Defrauded of Nearly 100 Lakhs
item.description: An accounts department phone was compromised in Kochi, allowing fraudsters to impersonate the chief executive officer on WhatsApp using his display picture and steal 99 lakh rupees.

item.title: Tunisian Court Sentences Opposition Figure to Four Years
item.description: Dual US-Tunisian citizen Olfa Hamdi received a four-year prison sentence for charges involving conspiracy and encouraging military insubordination through social media.

item.title: Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics Launches First Indigenous Survey
item.description: The Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics has initiated the nation's inaugural survey on ethnic minority communities to evaluate their socio-economic status and poverty levels, continuing through October 25.

item.title: JD Vance Comments on Republican Reactions to Ramaswamy Ad
item.description: Speaking in Cincinnati, vice-presidential figure JD Vance expressed displeasure with fellow Republicans regarding a disputed political advertisement. He stated his primary focus remains backing Republican candidates for upcoming midterm elections.

item.title: মার্কিন পররাষ্ট্রমন্ত্রী রুবিও জামনগরে রিলায়েন্স শোধনাগার পরিদর্শনে
item.description: মার্কিন পররাষ্ট্রমন্ত্রী মার্কো রুবিও গুজরাটের জামনগরে অবস্থিত রিলায়েন্সের তেল শোধনাগার দেখতে গেছেন। মার্কিন নির্বাচন ও ইরান সংঘাতের প্রেক্ষাপটে জ্বালানি তেলের বাজার স্থিতিশীল রাখাই এই সফরের প্রধান উদ্দেশ্য।

item.title: Pulwama hosts first office of RSS-linked labour union in Kashmir
item.description: The BMS, an organization tied to the RSS, inaugurated its inaugural office in Pulwama, Kashmir. A representative noted that the group has established 20 registered unions in the area following the 2020 revocation of Article 370. People initially misunderstood the RSS, but the union gained local acceptance over time.

item.title: Historic Manhattan townhouse featuring indoor pool priced at $10.45m
item.description: A 140-year-old Manhattan townhouse located at 238 West 74th Street is on the market for $10.45 million following a price reduction. Covering approximately 6,460 square feet, the residence includes six bedrooms, six and a half bathrooms, and a heated indoor swimming pool measuring 41 feet.

item.title: Kozhikode student dies after being struck by train
item.description: A female student in Kozhikode was fatally hit by the Thiruvananthapuram-bound Vande Bharat Express. According to police authorities, the incident occurred while she was trying to walk across the railway tracks.

item.title: Global website outages follow critical PHP security flaws discovered by AI
item.description: Websites around the globe went offline after artificial intelligence revealed severe vulnerabilities in PHP. Experts consider these programming language flaws to be unprecedented.

item.title: Aluva MLA defamation case registered against social media user
item.description: An individual has been formally charged with criminal defamation and related offenses. The case stems from allegations that the suspect posted defamatory content about the Aluva MLA on social media platforms.

item.title: মক্কা প্রতিরক্ষা চুক্তির মেয়াদ ও শর্ত ঘোষণা
item.description: নতুন এই চুক্তির প্রথম অনুচ্ছেদ অনুযায়ী, স্বাক্ষরকারী কোনো দেশের সার্বভৌমত্ব কিংবা সীমানা বিপন্ন হলে যৌথভাবে তা মোকাবিলা করা হবে। এছাড়া এই চুক্তি থেকে অন্তত দশ বছরের মধ্যে বেরিয়ে আসা যাবে না বলে শর্ত রয়েছে।

item.title: J&K High Court issues summons to Srinagar Deputy Commissioner
item.description: The High Court of Jammu and Kashmir summoned the Srinagar Deputy Commissioner regarding a Public Safety Act detention order. The court noted that the order appeared to lack proper judicial application of mind and specific factual details, requiring further scrutiny.

item.title: Delhi Police identify security flaws during safety audit
item.description: Delhi Police concluded a month-long security assessment covering roughly 1,600 parks and 3,000 schools across the city. The evaluation uncovered various vulnerabilities, such as damaged perimeter walls, defective surveillance cameras, and inadequate illumination.

item.title: Kuki-Zo Organizations Urge Restoration of President's Rule in Manipur
item.description: Kuki-Zo communities are pressing for President's Rule in Manipur once again. They report 32 fatalities in ethnic clashes since March, alongside ongoing economic blockades affecting their settlements.

item.title: Connecticut Renter Granted $1.6 Million Over Injury, Legal Counsel Claims Zero Payout
item.description: Michael Criscuolo secured a $1.6 million judgment after tripping over building waste outside his Connecticut rental. However, his attorney states the tenant has not received any funds despite the landlord's established negligence.

item.title: AfD Co-Leader Alice Weidel Outlines Extensive European Union Structural Changes
item.description: Alternative for Germany co-chair Alice Weidel has presented proposals for restructuring the European Union. In a separate event, Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang met with Berlin developers and investors.

item.title: Moscow Open to Restarting Negotiations With Kyiv and Washington
item.description: Russian leader Vladimir Putin indicated that Moscow is fundamentally prepared to restart diplomatic negotiations involving Ukraine and the United States following a visit by Witkoff.

item.title: Jammu Law Enforcement Dismantle Cross-Border Narcotics and Drone Smuggling Ring
item.description: Police in Jammu uncovered a cross-border drug operation, seizing 804 grams of heroin and 1.1 kilograms of opium. Authorities initiated the crackdown following the interrogation of a 26-year-old suspect.

item.title: Multiple Critical Security Flaws Discovered Across PHP, Node.js, and LiteLLM
item.description: Cybersecurity professionals face significant challenges following the discovery of software weaknesses in PHP, Node.js, and the LiteLLM platform, alongside new AI-identified vulnerabilities.

item.title: NFL Match Between Steelers and Saints Scheduled in Paris Amid Unrest
item.description: The National Football League game featuring the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will proceed in Paris on Sunday despite ongoing local civil unrest.

item.title: Tehran Rejects New Concessions on Uranium Holdings Amid Heightened Regional Tensions
item.description: Iran indicated it had no new responses for Washington following recent nuclear propositions delivered by intermediaries. Tehran remains resolved to retain its uranium reserves amid rising conflict risks.

item.title: J&K and Ladakh High Court Criticizes Ambiguous Detention Order
item.description: Justice Wasim Nargal emphasized that preventive detention requires strict procedural care and constitutional responsibility. The single bench questioned authorities regarding the vague categorization of detainees.

item.title: Afghanistan dismisses Bangladesh for 160
item.description: Strong batting from Ahmadzai and Omarzai helped establish a solid base as Bangladesh was bowled out for 160. Rashid Khan dismantled the lower order, helping Afghanistan claim the final six wickets for just 39 runs.
